entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Guillaume de La Jugie (born 1317 in Eyrein, Limousin; died May 6, 1374, in Avignon) was a prominent cardinal of the Catholic Church during the turbulent Avignon Papacy, directly related to two pontiffs. As the nephew of Pope Clement VI and the elder brother of Pope Gregory XI, his career exemplifies the powerful role of familial networks and curial administration in shaping the ecclesiastical landscape of 14th-century Europe. His ascent from a relatively obscure background to a position of immense influence within the papal court underscores the era's mechanisms of patronage and power consolidation, particularly within the French-dominated papacy.
